_about: Per-file style rolls for extract.py. Each roll picks one option by weight (seeded by file name) and fills {<roll>} and {<roll>_instruction} in that entity type's prompts. Weights within a roll are relative.

Standard.instruction: Usually 70-95 words. One or two short paragraphs.

Detailed.instruction: Usually 95-120 words. Use a short opening plus 2-3 bullets only when the one task has several distinct steps.

Overview first.instruction: Write as the organisation, in the first person plural. Open with one plain sentence on what the organisation does, at the level of a search-engine summary (e.g. "We are a [kind of organisation] in Singapore.", "We run a small chain of [businesses]."), then say what kind of specialist you need and for what.

Need first.instruction: Write as the organisation ("we", "our"). Open with the ask itself (e.g. "Looking for a [kind of specialist] to ...", "Seeking someone experienced in [field] to ..."), then mention what kind of organisation you are in a short clause or sentence, then the work.

Individual poster.instruction: Write as the one manager or owner posting the gig, using "I" and "my team" or "our" (e.g. "I look after [function] at a [kind of organisation] and need ..."). Don't invent a name or a job title the source doesn't support.

Context first.instruction: Open with one plain third-person sentence on what the organisation does (e.g. "A [kind of organisation] in Singapore is looking for ..."), then say what is needed. Avoid "we" throughout.

none.instruction: say only that it is in Singapore or operates locally; never name an estate, town or street. If the work needs a site visit, say it is on site in Singapore.

Labelled.instruction: start the sentence with "Deliverable:" and then name the output (e.g. "Deliverable: written gap analysis and prioritised action list.").

Natural.instruction: say what gets handed over in an ordinary sentence, without a "Deliverable:" label (e.g. "At the end we'd like a written gap analysis and a prioritised action list.", "The output is a working Excel model with a one-page guide.", "We expect a final report with the diagnosis and a corrective action plan."). It must still name the concrete output plainly.

Descriptive.instruction: State their core role and specialization plainly and factually -- no authority framing, no sales hook (e.g., "Senior Management Consultant specialising in supply chain transformation for Singapore retail clients").

Authority.instruction: Rewrite their core role as an official corporate/industry-leader title (e.g., "Former Head of [Field] & Industry Leader").

Value Prop.instruction: Rewrite their core role as a client-focused, benefit-driven hook (e.g., "Smart Financing as you Deserve").

Implied.instruction: Drop pronouns completely, as in a CV bullet: each sentence starts with a past-tense verb (e.g. "Led the migration of a client's payroll to a new platform.").

Direct First-Person.instruction: Use "I" with active verbs in each sentence (e.g. "I led the migration of a client's payroll to a new platform.").

none.instruction: none; use flawless grammar and punctuation.

double_connecting_word.instruction: Accidental double connecting word (e.g., "for the the project")

mid_sentence_tense_switch.instruction: Unintentionally switch grammatical tense mid-sentence (e.g., "led the team and develops new strategies")

omitted_trailing_period.instruction: Leave the final sentence without its period

none.instruction: none. Do not state what the service does not cover.

stated.instruction: end with one short sentence naming the nearest adjacent work a hirer might mistake this service for, which the source gives no sign the individual does (e.g. "Not focused on payroll or HR administration.", "Does not include legal drafting or court representation."). One adjacent area only, never a list.
